rationale: Room_swap and reverse both replay frames, so the crisp 'recur_frac>=0.9 => loop' rule was overriding the existing caveat and swallowing reverse (echo>10 with [300,480]) and A-B-A room_swaps; the typing guide now makes recurrence non-decisive, promotes echo>10 to reverse, and requires two opposed seams (jugde both big peaks) for room_swap so a single confirmation no longer types splice. Splice misses are addressed by naming the dominant photo_jump peak at a scenecut I-frame as a splice lead and by stressing that a confirmed break is strong positive evidence. dup_dense and extreme echo values are hedged so existing timewarp/reverse wins are not destabilized.

pack.task: Decide whether this 30s video clip was tampered with, and which candidates (if any) need a VLM continuity check.
pack.conclude_crit: stop gathering evidence and report the final verdict
pack.judge_crit_template: run the VLM continuity check on candidate {i} at frame {frame} (~{secs:.1f}s)

signals.recur_frac_max: fraction of frames that near-exactly replay an earlier frame (lag 2-10s). It CANNOT identify the type: a true loop, a reversed segment (frames replay in reverse) AND a swapped-in-then-returned scene (A-B-A: the return leg replays the pre-swap scene) all score high, so >=0.9 does NOT by itself mean loop. ~0.3-0.5 fits an A-B-A room_swap or a partially repeating scene; a static/frozen stretch also scores ~1.0. Corroborate with echo (reverse) or two opposed seams (room_swap) before naming a type.
signals.dup_dense_last_frame: last frame of a dense run of adjacent-duplicate frames. Non-null means a contiguous duplicate stretch exists and usually indicates timewarp (setpts slowdown); it can also come from a frozen/static swapped-in segment, so check whether the duplicated span is one scene played slow (timewarp) or a still inserted between two live scenes (room_swap). Null on clean/other.
signals.echo_best_score: self-anchored 4-factor score for a reversed segment: high only when TWO discontinuities echo each other (content after seam A matches content after seam B). A genuine reversed segment typically lands ~10-1e4 and should be preferred over loop even when recur_frac>=0.9 (reversal replays frames). Clean and other edits are typically <3; a pair existing with score<10 is NOT an echo; two discontinuities WITHOUT echo => room_swap or splice. Values so extreme they look degenerate (>1e6) usually mean near-static matches — corroborate locally instead of trusting them.
signals.scenecut_iframe_frames: frames where the video encoder inserted a scene-cut I-frame; flags abrupt visual discontinuity. BASE RATE: clean unedited clips average ~2-3 of these per 30s from natural motion, so a few are normal. A scene-cut I-frame coinciding (within a few frames) with the top photo_jump peak that motion cannot explain is the best free-signal hint of a same-scene splice — use it to justify a VLM check, not to conclude.
signals.photo_jump_top3: top frame-difference peaks. z is normalized WITHIN this clip, so the largest peak always scores high even on clean clips — read peak POSITIONS and co-occurrence, not z magnitude. An INSULATED peak that clearly dominates the runner-up and sits at a scene-cut I-frame is a splice lead; TWO comparable large peaks a few seconds apart are the signature of room_swap entry+return (judge both before typing splice).

pack.typing_guide: Recurrence signals cannot pick the type: loop, reverse and room_swap all replay frames, so recur_frac>=0.9 is NOT sufficient for loop. Decide structurally: echo_best_score>10 with two mirrored seams (sane range ~10-1e4) => reverse, overriding recur_frac>=0.9. recur_frac>=0.9 with a single fixed lag across the whole clip, no mirrored seams and no distinct intervening scene => loop. TWO judge-confirmed discontinuities seconds apart with echo<10, especially with a distinct intervening scene, => room_swap (the return leg replays the pre-swap scene, so recur_frac ~0.3-0.5 and a static/frozen stretch also fit room_swap). ONE confirmed discontinuity => splice (even if break_kind says scene_change) — but if a second equally large peak sits seconds away, judge it first: that pair means room_swap. No confirmed discontinuity + quiet signals => none. dup_dense_last_frame non-null points to a dense duplicate run (timewarp, or a frozen swap-in) and is not decisive alone.
pack.candidate_note: Each candidate is a suspicious transition the gates flagged. BASE RATE: the gates are permissive and nominate ~4-8 candidates per clip INCLUDING on clean clips, so a candidate existing is weak evidence — only its VLM verdict is strong evidence; a judge-confirmed discontinuity is strong evidence of corruption in the other direction too. Splice leaves NO free-signal trace and a same-scene cut is the case a judge can miss, so quiet signals do not rule it out: before concluding 'none', check the 2-3 strongest candidates, preferring the dominant photo_jump peak that coincides with a scenecut I-frame. For a room_swap lead, judge BOTH of the two largest peaks when they are seconds apart — one confirmation alone looks like splice. A judge call costs ~2s; a handful of well-chosen checks is enough, then conclude.

questions.action: What is the best next step?
questions.corrupted: This clip contains an artificial temporal discontinuity (an edit: replayed footage, reversed segment, swapped scene, cut/splice, or retimed segment). One confirmed break is sufficient.
questions.break_type: Which edit type best fits the evidence?
questions.sufficient: The current evidence is sufficient to conclude with confidence; more VLM checks would not change the verdict.
questions.is_type_template: The evidence indicates this clip was edited with a {type} corruption ({desc}).

type_desc.loop: footage repeats itself — a segment is replayed
type_desc.reverse: a segment plays backward in time (two mirrored seams)
type_desc.room_swap: the scene changes to a different place and later returns to the original (A-B-A)
type_desc.splice: a hard cut joins non-contiguous footage of the same scene (no replay)
type_desc.timewarp: part of the clip plays at altered speed (slowed or sped up)
